- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥ 0.67 or 1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤ 0.33) within 5 days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply +1–2% bias to first 5–7 days.
- If recent 5-day average price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; adjust forecast to align with 5-day moving average for next 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lag correction (forecast = true value from 2–3 days prior) for next 5–7 days.
